title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 151 (Care to be taken by bailee)

content.overview: Section 151 provides that in all cases of bailment the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value as the goods bailed.
content.glance: The bailee must take the care that a man of ordinary prudence would take of his own similar goods under similar circumstances.
content.study: In all cases of bailment the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value as the goods bailed. Current-law framing: the standard is that of ordinary prudence, not absolute liability; it applies to all bailments.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: In all cases of bailment the bailee is bound to take as much care of the goods bailed to him as a man of ordinary prudence would, under similar circumstances, take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value as the goods bailed.

examples.title: Ordinary prudence
examples.body: A bailee storing goods must take the same care a reasonably prudent person would take of his own goods of similar bulk, quality and value under the same circumstances.

hypotheticals.question: Does the standard of care differ between gratuitous and non-gratuitous bailment?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 151 applies the ordinary-prudence standard in all cases of bailment.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 151 requires the bailee, in every bailment, to take as much care of the goods as a man of ordinary prudence would take of his own goods of the same bulk, quality and value under similar circumstances. The standard is that of ordinary prudence, not insurer-like absolute liability.
examples: Reasonable precautions appropriate to the goods and circumstances satisfy the section.
distinctions: Section 151 states the affirmative duty of care; Section 152 protects the bailee who has taken that care (absent special contract).
problemApplication: Identify the circumstances and nature of the goods.
Conclude whether the required care was taken.
keyTakeaways: Bailee must take ordinary prudent care of similar goods under similar circumstances.
